sections.history: Keezhaparasalur, a village in Mayiladuthurai district between Mayiladuthurai and Thirukkadaiyur, is the Thirupariyalur of the Tevaram hymns. Its temple to Shiva as Veerateeswarar, also called Dakshapureeswarar, is one of the eight Ashta Veerattanams — the shrine of the Lord's judgement on Daksha. Sambandar sang a hymn on the Lord of Thirupariyalur, and the temple is counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams of the Chola country. Its present masonry is assigned to the Chola period, with later expansions under the Thanjavur Nayaks. The temple keeps four worship services through the day and remains a place of quiet devotion in the delta countryside.
sections.architecture: The temple is a compact Dravidian shrine of the Kaveri delta, its gateway opening onto a courtyard around the sanctum of Veerateeswarar, with the goddess Ilangombanaiyal in a shrine of her own. What sets it apart is the honour given to the deed itself: Daksha Samhara Murthy is worshipped here, and Veerabhadra, the fierce form who carried out the Lord's judgement, has a shrine of his own — among the earliest temples, some hold, to give him such a place.
sections.legends: Daksha, father of the goddess Sati, held a great sacrifice and invited every god but Shiva, his own son-in-law. Sati went to her father's house unbidden and, hearing her Lord insulted, gave up her life in the sacrificial fire. In grief and fury Shiva sent forth Veerabhadra, who scattered the assembly and destroyed the sacrifice, and Daksha's pride was broken. Tradition holds that when Daksha was restored to life with the head of a goat, he bowed before the Lord he had scorned — and Thirupariyalur keeps that moment of judgement turned to grace.
sections.festivals: The festivals of the Shaiva year are kept here — Maha Shivaratri, the fortnightly pradosham, Arudra Darshan in Margazhi and Karthigai Deepam — with special worship at Veerabhadra's shrine. Pilgrims on the Veerattanam circuit often time their visit with the larger festivals of nearby Thirukkadaiyur; confirm dates locally.
sections.experience: Thirupariyalur is a village temple among paddy fields, visited mostly by those who seek it out. It is a place to reflect on pride and its undoing: the Lord who would not be shut out of the sacrifice, and the proud king who learned humility. It lies a short drive from Thirukkadaiyur, and the two Veerattanams are usually visited on the same day.

visit.timings: Open daily in morning and evening sessions with a midday closure, as at most village temples of the delta. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left outside before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is not permitted inside the sanctum; in the outer corridors, ask the temple staff before taking pictures, especially of rituals and the festival bronzes.
visit.gettingThere: Keezhaparasalur lies in Mayiladuthurai district, roughly midway between Mayiladuthurai and Thirukkadaiyur and about 10 km from each, off the Mayiladuthurai–Tharangambadi road. Mayiladuthurai is the nearest railhead; Tiruchirappalli is the nearest large airport.
